messages: support_lead: @oncall heads-up — Acme Payments hitting intermittent 429s + latency spikes since 09:12 UTC. Customer reports it started after a large billing job at ~09:00. They see "rate_limit_exceeded" errors and the long tail on token latency. Need ownership for triage and attribution (route vs model vs customer quota) and a quick mitigation plan. oncall: I'm on it. Can you drop sample request-ids / headers from the customer? Need x-client-id, x-rate-limit-* headers, and any request IDs. support_lead: pasted two request IDs from the customer: req_8a1c and req_f3b2. They included x-client-id: acme-payments, model: gpt-j-6b, route: /v1/generate. They attached a few truncated logs. kira: Triage plan: 1) confirm whether quota counters for acme were exhausted, 2) check if gpt-j-6b backend hosts surfaced queueing or OOMs, 3) verify routing/fallback behavior. I'll pull usage aggregates + infra metrics. sam: Quick Datadog queries to slice 429s by route/customer: avg(last_5m):sum:request.errors{http.status:429}.as_count() by {route,customer_id}.rollup(sum,60) Also check header trends: x-rate-limit-remaining and x-rate-limit-reset in logs. Example log from their upload: {"ts":"2025-11-03T09:12:04Z","req":"req_8a1c","status":429,"route":"/v1/generate","model":"gpt-j-6b","customer_id":"acme-payments","error":"rate_limit_exceeded"} ashley: Repro steps for ops that I used locally: 1) curl using customer key: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXX" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":1024}' 2) inspect response headers: x-rate-limit-remaining, x-rate-limit-limit, x-rate-limit-reset. Customer saw: x-rate-limit-remaining: 0, x-rate-limit-limit: 1000, x-rate-limit-reset: 1699075920. max: Quick mitigation suggestions: temporary quota bump for acme or enable a short burst window while we investigate. Also route non-critical calls to a smaller model (gpt-j-3b) as fallback to reduce GPU queueing. I'll prepare an emergency token adjustment if owners approve. oncall: Pulled usage table and found a huge spike. Query I ran: SELECT customer_id, route, count(*) as calls, sum(tokens) as tokens FROM usage.events WHERE ts between '2025-11-03 09:00' and '2025-11-03 09:20' GROUP BY customer_id, route ORDER BY calls desc; Result: acme-payments -> /v1/generate -> ~12,000 calls in 5m, primarily model=gpt-j-6b. Tokens spiked accordingly. Attribution looks customer-driven, not a model-side cascade. support_lead: Also saw backend latency increases. p95/p99 for model gpt-j-6b rose and GPU host queue lengths increased; might be hitting Dedicated pool concurrency. Eng-runtime should check kernel queueing and batch size behavior. sam: Recommended dashboard panels to add/update: - 429s by customer/route (top 20) - token burn rate per customer (1m / 5m) - x-rate-limit-remaining heatmap by customer - model latency p95/p99 by backend host Suggested alerts: - Datadog monitor: when 429s/min for a single customer > 5 => paging to eng oncall - When GPU queue length > threshold or model node CPU% sustained high => page infra - When token rate for customer > 3x baseline for 5m => warn support. oncall: I've manually bumped acme bump window +20% for 30m and enabled fallback routing from gpt-j-6b -> gpt-j-3b for non-streaming routes. Customer reports a drop in 429s after ~3 minutes. support_lead: Action items assigned: - eng-runtime (owner: kira): investigate kernel queueing and whether batching/quantization changes caused regressions on gpt-j-6b hosts. - billing (owner: max): verify auto-throttle and quota configuration for acme, and confirm whether the billing job triggered an expected throttle. - support (owner: support_lead): send timeline and mitigation summary to customer; include temporary quota change and fallback routing. - devex/docs (owner: ashley): draft a KB + dashboard snippet showing dd queries and cURL repro. rate-limiter-bot: Incident annotated — incident_id: INC-20251103-042, severity: low, runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/quota-attribution ashley: I'll assemble the post-incident dashboard tiles and a KB article with the Datadog monitor JSON + cURL repro steps. Will link to runbook and include example queries. support_lead: Thanks team — keep me posted if latency resurges. I'll close after we have the postmortem note and customer's confirmation. :thumbsup:
